steps.title: Protected is not always safe
steps.body: A piece with a defender can still be lost if the attacker is worth less. A pawn attacking a knight wins the knight for a pawn even when the knight is protected. Count what you win and what you lose.
White's knight on e4 is protected by the pawn on d3. The black pawn on d5 attacks it.

steps.q: Is the knight on e4 safe?
options: No, a pawn takes a knight and they only lose a pawn back
steps.why: Pawn (1) for knight (3): they come out two points ahead.

steps.q: Your rook (5) takes a pawn (1) that is protected by a pawn. What happens?
options: You lose the rook for a pawn
steps.why: You gain 1 and lose 5, so you are down 4.

steps.body: Here Rxd5 looks tempting, but exd5 follows. Count first.

cards.prompt: A piece is protected. Is it always safe?
solution: No, a cheaper attacker still wins it.
